Updated assessment with Beige Book insights:
- FOMC (May 3, 2023): Modest growth, robust jobs, elevated inflation; policy tightened to 5–5.25% and balance-sheet runoff continues; credit tightening expected to weigh on activity and inflation.
- SLOOS (April 2023): Broad tightening of standards/terms across C&I, CRE, and consumer credit; weaker loan demand; banks expect further tightening—amplifying downside risks to growth and hiring.
- Beige Book: On balance, activity was largely flat to slightly positive—growth reported in only a few Districts while most saw little change; consumer spending mixed with auto sales steady; price growth described as moderate; reports of declining lending volumes and weaker loan demand reinforce credit headwinds.

Implication: The Beige Book corroborates tighter credit and softer loan demand while showing only limited growth across Districts. This increases downside risk to real activity relative to the FOMC’s “modest” expansion narrative, even as price pressures moderate and some consumer categories remain steady. Netting these, sentiment is nudged further negative.

sentiment score = -0.33
